draft.title: Draft Note: Combining Energy Models and Textual Gradients
draft.content: Rough initial idea: Maybe we can use energy-based models together with textual gradients to optimize text documents. Energy models assign low energy to good states, and LLM critics can write critiques to improve a draft.

draft.title: Draft Note: Combining Energy Models and Textual Gradients
draft.content: Rough initial idea: Maybe we can use energy-based models together with textual gradients to optimize text documents. Energy models assign low energy to good states. An energy function scores candidate states, and Boltzmann-based sampling explores candidates rather than only selecting the current best one, connecting this approach to [[Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning]]. More specifically, the energy function ranks candidate states, while MCMC sampling explores alternatives; this distinction connects to [[Guided Cost Learning: Deep Inverse Optimal Control]] and [[Training Products of Experts by Minimizing Contrastive Divergence]]. LLM critics can write critiques to improve a draft. A critic can diagnose a specific failure, propose a discrete edit, and then evaluate that edit, as in [[TextGrad: Automatic Differentiation via Text]] and [[ProTeGi: Prompt Optimization with Textual Gradients]]. Varied edits can help avoid local stagnation, but discrete edit diversity does not imply well-mixed Langevin chains; short-run chains can remain poorly mixed without KL shaping, as discussed in [[Lab Notebook #42: Why Short-Run K=10 Langevin Chains Fail Without KL Shaping]].

task2_adversarial_hard_negative.title: Allosteric Folding and Ribosomal Proofreading in a Shared Free-Energy Landscape
task2_adversarial_hard_negative.key_equation: P(s) = exp[-βG(s)] / Z, where Z = Σ_s exp[-βG(s)] and G(s) includes conformational and ligand-binding contributions
task2_adversarial_hard_negative.content:
Allosteric proteins distribute among conformational states according to their free energies: the Boltzmann weights of those states are normalized by the partition function Z. Ligand binding shifts that partition, changing the occupancy of active and inactive structures without requiring a change in the protein’s covalent sequence. In a folding intermediate, a solvent-exposed inner-loop can couple a distant binding pocket to the catalytic site; its backbone flexibility contributes to the conformational ensemble and to the rate of transition between states.

A Langevin description of this motion treats solvent collisions as stochastic forces acting on the protein’s coordinates while preserving the appropriate free-energy landscape. The resulting trajectories can reveal how a ligand stabilizes one basin and alters the probability of productive folding. Along a polypeptide, the textual gradient of residue identities—read here as the ordered biochemical sequence of amino acids and their changing side-chain properties—can be compared with the physical gradient of hydrophobic exposure as folding proceeds.

A related selectivity problem occurs during ribosomal proofreading. The decoding center gives molecular attention to the geometry of codon–anticodon pairing: near-cognate tRNAs are more likely to dissociate before accommodation, while cognate pairing favors forward progression. This kinetic critique is biochemical selection, not an editorial judgment: it reflects differential binding, conformational rearrangement, and GTP-coupled steps. Together, allosteric folding and translational proofreading show how molecular ensembles partition among competing states and how selective transitions enrich functional outcomes.

It does not connect energy-based scoring and stochastic candidate sampling to discrete natural-language critique and editing, and it contains no required wiki-links or discussion of short-run sampling and edit-stagnation risks.

task3_cross_domain_reenactment.title: Section 5.4 Re-Enactment: Normalized Cluster State and Bounded-Round Consensus
task3_cross_domain_reenactment.key_equation: Z_C = Σ_{s∈S_C} exp[-E_C(s)]; q(x) = α q_gossip(x) + (1−α) q_replay(x); s_{t+1} ~ p_C(·|s_t), t=0,…,K−1, with rollout objective D_KL(Q_K || P_C); g_θ(u,v) = A_θ(u,v) · V_qc(u,v)
task3_cross_domain_reenactment.content:
This architecture treats a replicated cluster’s admissible configurations as a global state space S_C. Each configuration s has an energy E_C(s) encoding protocol constraints, such as log consistency, membership rules, and safety conditions. The cluster state normalizer Z_C sums the weights of all admissible configurations, giving a normalized distribution over global states rather than independent local-node beliefs.

To propose candidate states efficiently, the protocol mixes two sources: q_gossip, which assembles proposals from recent peer exchanges, and q_replay, which resamples logged transitions or previously observed recovery traces. The mixture q supports importance-weighted evaluation of rare but consequential configurations while retaining coverage of states suggested by current gossip traffic.

From a current state, the coordinator performs a bounded K-round gossip rollout. At each round, nodes exchange state summaries and update their local candidate view; the rollout distribution Q_K is shaped toward the protocol-consistent target P_C by a KL divergence objective. The bound K limits communication and decision latency, while the divergence term discourages rollout proposals that depart too far from the target cluster-state distribution.

Finally, a pairwise attention gate assigns weight A_θ(u,v) to the relationship between a proposer u and verifier v, using context such as membership, recency, and observed message consistency. The pairwise quorum-certificate verifier V_qc(u,v) checks signatures, voting eligibility, and certificate compatibility. Their combination g_θ(u,v) makes pairwise quorum-certificate verification the acceptance critic: a candidate transition is admitted only when relevant pairwise evidence is sufficiently weighted and the required quorum conditions hold. Thus normalization, proposal generation, bounded rollout, and pairwise verification form one relational pipeline for consensus-state selection.

correspondence_mapping.systems_enact: Cluster state normalizer Z_C over admissible global replicated configurations

independent_isomorphism_evaluation.critic_verification: The re-enactment closely preserves the global state normalizer, bounded K-step rollout with KL shaping, and attention-gated pairwise verification. Its main representation gap is that the proposal mixture is described with importance-weighted evaluation and coverage, but does not specify the contrastive estimation objective itself; rollout coverage calibration is also less explicit than its KL term.
